title: An inductor responds slowly
hook: Change inductance and predict RL time constant.
misconception: RL time constant stays fixed when inductance doubles.
objective: Apply τ = L/R to compare RL time constant when inductance changes, under the stated assumptions.

claims.text: With an ideal series RL circuit with fixed resistance, τ = L/R. When inductance doubles, RL time constant becomes 2 times its original value.
claims.source: Idealized model τ = L/R; scaling exponent 1. Physics and assumptions await independent review.

recall.question: Consider an ideal series RL circuit with fixed resistance, with a nonzero initial result. If inductance triples from a positive value, what is the multiplier on RL time constant?
recall.why: Apply τ = L/R under the same assumptions: the multiplier is 3.
